- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of downward trend in forecast to align with momentum.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +1.00 after -1.00), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% in next 2–3 days to capture sentiment shift.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates upward momentum in early weeks; apply a 1–2% upward bias in first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If true outcome shows persistent divergence from model (e.g., >3% error over 5+ days), apply a “reversion buffer” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence or sentiment stabilizes.
